question: An alternating current of [[1.5 mA|2]] and angular frequency [[300 rad/s|2]] flows through a [[10 kΩ|3]] resistor and a [[0.50 μF|3]] capacitor [[in series|1]]. Find the [[rms voltage across the capacitor|4]] and also calculate the [[impedance of the circuit|5]].
steps: Let's first understand the question.
A resistor and a capacitor are connected in series, so this is an R C series circuit.
An alternating current of one point five milliampere flows through it, with angular frequency three hundred radian per second.
The resistance is ten kilo ohm, and the capacitance is zero point five microfarad.
We have to find two things. First, the rms voltage across the capacitor.
Second, the impedance of the whole circuit.
Let's solve it step by step.
Look at the circuit. R and C are in series, so the same current, one point five milliampere, flows through both of them.
The A C source has angular frequency three hundred radian per second.
A capacitor opposes alternating current through its reactance. X C equals one by omega C.
In series, R and X C are at right angles, so the impedance Z equals root of R square plus X C square.
And the voltage across the capacitor is V C equals I into X C.
Now put the values. Omega is three hundred, and C is zero point five into ten to the power minus six farad.
So X C equals one by three hundred into zero point five into ten to the power minus six.
That gives X C about six point six seven kilo ohm.
Now the impedance. Z equals root of ten to the power four whole square, plus six point six seven into ten to the power three whole square.
This gives Z about one point two into ten to the power four ohm.
And V C equals one point five into ten to the power minus three, into six point six seven into ten to the power three.
So V C is ten volt.
Now let's check the options. Option B gives ten to the power four volt, which is far too big.
Option C ignores the capacitive reactance.
Option D gives an impedance of only ten ohm, which is far too small.
Only option A matches both values.
So the correct answer is option A.
Ten volt across the capacitor, and impedance one point two into ten to the power four ohm.
